correctness.rationale: The exact support-width formula follows from Minkowski additivity for interval simplices. Gaussian radial projection gives the precise chi-(n-1) normalization. Standard Mills ratios yield independent upper/lower Poisson exceedance processes; bounded-away-from-diagonal weighted sums converge after finite-mark truncation; the uniform absolute-moment bound E|normalized M_k|<=C(1+log(n/k)) makes the diagonal vanish, and the Poisson log-length expectation is integrable. Chi concentration removes radial noise at order (log n)/sqrt(n). A high positive-mark insertion gives a strictly exponential lower bound on the right tail of the limiting law, precluding normality. The delivered checker passed 159 independent finite support tests and 12 mean tests. Simulation does not substitute for the limit proof.

originality.rationale: The actual sources establish the interval-simplex construction and nested fan (Postnikov; Padrol--Pilaud--Poullot), and Gaussian mean widths/Gumbel limits of individual regular polytopes (Kabluchko--Litvak--Zaporozhets), not the jointly dependent sum over all overlapping interval simplices. The new assessed statement is the profile-uniform spatial Poisson integral limit with non-Gaussianity and a computable second-order mean correction. Exact finite means follow known additivity and are not independently asserted novel. published-finding corpus comparisons and accessible own claims found no implication covering the result, but broad integrated-scan-extreme terminology remains a genuine residual originality risk.

value.rationale: The main mathematical invariant is the intrinsic Euclidean width distribution for the classical associahedron family and its positive interval-weight deformations. Strongly overlapping interval-simplex summands produce a non-Gaussian limit driven by spatially shared extremes, robust for every fixed positive continuous profile. The explicit profile-dependent mean correction and canonical numerical value have clear interpretive significance for the first intrinsic-volume geometry; neither the limit distribution nor its robustness is a textbook single-simplex computation. No volume/inradius/normal-fan statement is inflated into novelty.
